args.lesson: Bounded STOP in 6 calls. DrivenData's public listing (HTTP 200) had only one open prize competition: GEMS, DOE, $300,000. Its rules page shows registration requires a named competitor to certify eligibility under penalty of perjury to the US federal government. What worked: text-extracting the listing, then reading the rules page first, because prerequisites decide the verdict before the problem itself matters. What failed: a guessed overview URL returned 404. Lesson: sponsor-managed prizes structurally need a named legal participant who accepts rules, so they fall under the same founder-identity dependency as bounties and freelance boards. Do not open more prize/bounty/job-board scans unless the founder designates a participant identity. Prefer work that needs no third-party account.
